questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For an octahedral complex ${MX}_{4}{Y}_{2}$ (M = a$ transition metal, $X$ and $Y$ are monodentate achiral ligands), the correct statement among the following is$
options: ${MX}_{4}{Y}_{2}$ has $2$& geometrical isomers, one of which is chiral
${MX}_{4}{Y}_{2}$ has $2$ geometrical isomers both of which are achiral
${MX}_{4}{Y}_{2}$ has $4$ geometrical isomers, all of which are achiral
${MX}_{4}{Y}_{2}$ has $4$ geometrical isomers, two of which are chiral
questions.solution:
Two geometrical isomers (cis and trans with respect to ligand $Y$) are possible. The trans isomer has both centre of symmetry and several planes of symmetry.

and, therefore it is achiral.

The cis isomer has two planes of symmetry and, therefore it is also achiral.

questions.q: Among the following, the pair of paramagnetic complexes is&
questions.solution:
${K}_{3} \left[Fe \left(CN\right)^{6}\right]$

Central metal ion is ${Fe}^{3 +}$, which has $\left[Ar\right]3d^{5}$ configuration as free ion. In strong ligand field of ${CN}^{-}$, its splits to become ${t}_{2g} eg0 5$.

One unpaired electron will be there, and 

$∴$ It is paramagnetic.

${K}_{3} \left[{CoF}_{6}\right]$: Central metal ion is ${Co}^{3 +}$.

Free metal ion configuration $\left[Ar\right]3d^{6}$.

In weak ligand field of $F^{-}$, its splits and becomes ${t}_{2g}^{4}{e}_g^{2}$.

Four unpaired electrons, therefore paramagnetic.

In ${K}_{4} \left[Fe \left(CN\right)^{6}\right]$, central ion is ${Fe}^{2 +}$ and in \l$ left[Co \left({NH}_{3}\right)6\right]{Cl}_{3}$, central ion is ${Co}^{3 +}$

In both of them, free metal ion is $\left(Ar\right)3d^{6}$.

Ligands ${NH}_{3}$ and ${CN}^{-}$ are of strong field, ${Δ}_{0} > P$

So, $d^{6}$ splits to ${t}_{2g}^{6}{e}_g^{0}$

No unpaired electrons, therefore diamagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The complex having the highest spin only magnetic moment is
questions.solution:
The spin only magnetic moment for a complex can be calculated using formula

$\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}$

(a) $\left[Fe\left(CN\right)6\right]3 -$

The oxidation number Fe in $\left[Fe\left(CN\right)6\right]3 -$ is $+ 3$ .The electronic configuration of ${Fe}^{3 +}$ is $- \left(Ar\right)3d^{5}4s^{0}$

As ${CN}^{-}$ is a strong ligand pairing will occur.

$\left[Fe\left(CN\right)6\right]3 -$

$∴ n = 1 ⇒ \mu = \sqrt{1\left(1 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{3}$

(b) $\left[Fe\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]2 +$

The oxidation number of $Fe$ in

$\left[Fe\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]2 +$ is $+ 2$ .The electronic configuration of ${Fe}^{2 +}$ is $- \left[Ar\right]3d^{6}4s^{0}$

As ${H}_{2}O$ is weak ligand, so pairing will not occur.

$\left[Fe\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]2 -$


$n = 4$

$\mu = \sqrt{4\left(4 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{24}$

(c) $\left[{MnF}_{6}\right]4 -$

The oxidation number of $Mn$ is $+ 2$. It's
configuration is $- \left[Ar\right]3d^{5}4s^{0}$

As $F^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so pairing will not occur.

$\left[{MnF}_{6}\right]4 -$


$n = 5$

$\mu = \sqrt{5\left(5 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{35}$

(d) $\left[{NiCl}_{4}\right]2 -$

In ${NiCl}_{4}^{2 -}$, the oxidation number of $Ni$ will be $+ 2 .$ It's configuration is $- \left[Ar\right]3d^{8}4s^{0}$

As ${Cl}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so pairing will not occur.

$\left[{NiCl}_{4}\right]2 -$

$n = 2$

$\mu = \sqrt{2\left(2 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{8}$

Thus, $\left[{MnF}_{6}\right]4 -$ will have the highest spin only magnetic moment.

(i) $\mathrm{Co}^{+3}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{6} \mathrm{~s}^{0}\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is a strong field ligand

(iii) $\mathrm{Cr}^{+3}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{3} 4 \mathrm{~s}^{0}\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand
(iv) $\mathrm{Fe}^{+2}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{6} 4 \mathrm{~s}^{0}\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand.
So, $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{3}$ will be diamagnetic.
